findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope AC5's grep to contributor-facing prose (docs/, guides, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) and exclude the src/ matcher code, OR add an explicit allow-list for the `_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` definition line so the retired-word detector is not flagged.
evidence: Design: 'Add `_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` for the old word.'
AC5: 'grep -rn "recheck-review" docs/ src/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md infra/ returns no contributor instruction (only the historical ADR/ticket record, if any).'
The retired-token regex source in src/ necessarily embeds the old word string, so a src/ grep for it matches required code.
findings.finding: AC5's proving command `grep -rn "recheck-review" ... src/ ...` will match the `_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` definition that retrigger.py MUST contain to detect and refuse the retired word; the AC's exemption only covers 'historical ADR/ticket record', not live matcher code, so the command cannot return empty even on a correct implementation.
scenarios: Executor runs AC5 grep; it returns the retrigger.py regex line; AC appears to fail despite correct implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Split AC5: assert no contributor instruction in docs/AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md via grep, and separately assert src/ contains the retired word ONLY in the `_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` definition (e.g. `grep -rn recheck-review src/ | grep -v _RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` returns empty).

evidence: verify command `grep -rn "recheck-review" docs/ src/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md infra/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable

verify command `grep -rn "recheck-review" docs/ src/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md infra/` returns` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable

findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make AC5 deterministic: either exclude the historical-record paths from the grep target set explicitly, or assert grep returns empty over a precisely enumerated contributor-doc path set.
evidence: AC5: 'returns no contributor instruction (only the historical ADR/ticket record, if any)'
A raw `grep -rn` returns all matches; the AC then applies a subjective 'is this instruction vs history' judgment with no deterministic filter.
findings.finding: AC5's success condition ('returns no contributor instruction (only the historical ADR/ticket record, if any)') requires a human to interpret grep output rather than a deterministic pass/fail, so the criterion is not mechanically evaluable.
scenarios: A historical ADR still contains the retired word; grep is non-empty; whether AC5 passes depends on manual classification.
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact excluded historical paths (e.g. `--exclude-dir=docs/adr` or exclude the specific ADR file) so the grep is expected to return exactly zero lines on success.

findings.finding: The TRIGGER_TOKEN / _TOKEN_RE rename inventory omits the test files that carry the retired word 'recheck-review' as string literals. tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py hardcodes it as the _comment_event default (line 52) and at line 265; these feed the accepted path, which after the hard cutover routes 'recheck-review' to the refusal branch, breaking every accepted-path assertion. The plan's inventory lists only 'retrigger.py' and 'Docs/guides/runbooks/comments' — neither covers these test files, and such string-literal usages are invisible to LSP structural reference lookup and require a separate grep sweep.

tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py:277 (test_token_word_match_positive_forms) and :261 (near-miss list) — hardcoded 'recheck-review' literals must be re-authored to 'rerun-llm-review' / its near-misses; AC1 implies this for :261 but the positive-form and attestation-file literals are not enumerated in the plan's affected-file list.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the change list: 'tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger_attestation_6a81.py and tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py — replace hardcoded `recheck-review` trigger literals with `rerun-llm-review` (accepted-path fixtures) and update near-miss parametrizations to the new word'; note these are string literals found by grepping the word, not by symbol-reference lookup.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the retired-token refusal branch resolves change_id/revision before it calls post_comment — either re-anchor via get_change_event first, or order the retired refusal after that resolution — so the AC2 'exactly one refusal reply' is postable.
evidence: Plan: 'loop guard -> new-token match -> retired-token match (refusal branch) -> project guard -> eligibility -> reset. The retired branch ... posts exactly one best-effort post_comment refusal and returns None.'

Code: change_id/revision are resolved by the get_change_event re-anchor at retrigger.py:318-342, which runs after the project guard (306-309); the existing refusal post at line 377 consumes those resolved values.
post_comment signature requires (change_id, revision, message) — see test at tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py:303 client.post_comment('rebar~main~Iabc', 'rev2', 'hello').
findings.finding: The plan places the retired-token refusal branch (which posts a comment) before the project guard and before the eligibility re-anchor, but post_comment requires a resolved revision that the current code only derives from get_change_event AFTER the project guard.
scenarios: A comment carrying the retired word arrives before the branch has resolved change_id/revision, so the refusal branch has no revision to post on.
AC2 requires 'posts exactly one refusal reply' but the ordering makes the revision source undefined.

findings.checklist_item: Decide whether the retired-token refusal should be gated by the project guard; if so, order the project guard ahead of the retired refusal branch (or state the intent to reply cross-project and why it is safe).
evidence: Plan order places 'retired-token match (refusal branch)' before 'project guard'.
Code: the project guard (retrigger.py:306-309) returns None with no comment posted for foreign projects; every post_comment call is downstream of it.
findings.finding: Ordering the retired-token refusal before the project guard causes the bot to post refusal comments on changes in projects it does not own, a behavioral regression from the current code which posts nothing until after the project guard.
scenarios: A retired-word comment lands on a change in a project outside cfg.project; the bot posts a refusal there.
